one_line: Browser-local agent control and telemetry for ESP32 firmware development.
what_it_does: Streams live board telemetry, runs measured experiments, builds firmware, and gates flashing on human approval.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP reaches a USB-connected board while sharing live telemetry and approval state; ordinary UI automation cannot comparably provide structured closed-loop hardware control.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes live measurements, iterative experiments, firmware builds, and approval-gated flashing.
About text ties the browser tab's JavaScript to the serial link and shared board state.
Frames show laptop, cable, physical board, code, and test overlays.
execution_rationale: Coherent hardware-agent loop with baseline harness, telemetry, measurement, source review, and human gate; not every claimed flow is independently visible.
execution_evidence: 128-second video transcript describes end-to-end workflow.
Frames show physical electronics connected to a laptop and performance measurements.
Facts report live demo and public repository.
impact_rationale: Firmware developers have a costly edit-flash-observe-debug loop that this product directly addresses with measured feedback and safer writes.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies the agent visibility gap in hardware development.
Transcript describes temperature, frame-rate, and reboot feedback.
creativity_rationale: It extends browser-native agent collaboration into physical hardware with a shared-observer model and measured experimentation.
creativity_evidence: Agent sees the board it programs through a persistent harness.
Combines telemetry, experiments, firmware generation, and approval gating.
usability_note: Clear workflow and approval gate, but hardware setup is specialized.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP delta, credible physical demo, and high-value workflow.
